text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Official: Netanyahu-Arafat summit a must. Arafat meets Jewish settlers.
- Crash survivor hospitalised on return home.
- Ottawa ready to probe new list of Nazi war criminals in Canada.
- Girl from hepatitis-stricken village gets first live-donor liver transplant.
- Avner, the compulsory car insurer, lacks sufficient capital to stay in market.
- Experts to government: Don't retreat from "options plan" meant to sell state assets to general public through voucher scheme.
- Oil Refineries moves into red despite massive layoffs.
GLOBES
- Chase Manhattan freezes plans to set up mission in Israel because of political situation.
HAARETZ
- Special U.N. committee on Israeli behaviour in the territories says it reflects a sadistic culture.
- Syrian foreign minister Shara: At beginning of year we reached agreements on principles with Israel on a withdrawal from the Golan Heights.
- Health Ministry has confidential list of 12,000 people who underwent radiation treatment against ringworm in the 1950s and most of them don't know they're in danger.
- Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel: We are acting based on an inflation target of 8 to 10 percent in 1997.
MAARIV
- Israeli President Ezer Weizman mediates between Netanyahu and Arafat, sends his director-general to the talks on Hebron and calls both Netanyahu and the Palestinians.
- Netanyahu: It could be the cut in the budget will exceed 7 billion shekels.
- Israel Electric Co asks to raise rates by another 7.4 percent.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Flexibility in Israeli stance; optimism on Hebron negotiations.
- Couscous now on Israeli army menu.
